doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Bass playing, avant-garde and the state of the music
title: Avant-garde audiences
summary: Ware says the public is not supposed to understand avant-garde music and goes along with the image.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: You're kind of used to seeing that in the neighborhood, moreso, it seemed, where you'd go in and you may get a star working with some local guys and they may not be able to play [it's author?] music. But this is more far-reaching than that, because these are people that are on the national scene, so to speak.
The avantgarde people, you speaking of?

Well, yes, they up there. But that's what they -- they supposed to be -- avantgarde, the average public ain't supposed to understand nothing they're playing. It's a so way out. Most of the public don't understand, but they're going along with the images. "Yes, I know exactly what's happening." And the guy's standing up there, just take a deep breath and blow a whole lot of notes, and that's it.
